Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Houston/Galveston TX
707 PM CDT Fri Jul 31 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES...

- A cold front will bring a chance for a few showers and
  thunderstorms Saturday afternoon/evening through very early
  Sunday. 
 
- Next week's outlook features seasonably hot and humid conditions
  with isolated afternoon showers and storms possible.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 212 PM CDT Fri Jul 31 2026

Summer persists in Southeast Texas as hot and humid conditions
continue thanks to high pressure and abundant sunshine.
Temperatures this afternoon have rising into the mid 90s for much
of the region with heat indices in the 100-105 degree range.
Another warm and muggy night is expected tonight, but then on
Saturday I have something to discuss that isn't just high pressure
and heat. An upper-level disturbance moving through the Midwest
will push a weak "cold" front into Southeast Texas tomorrow into
tomorrow night. Because the front is so weak, exact FROPA timing
is still uncertain - but it will likely be in the late afternoon
into the evening hours from north to south. Isolated showers will
begin to pop up across the Piney Woods region as early as the 
morning hours as the front approaches from the north. By the
afternoon and into the evening hours, isolated to scattered
showers and thunderstorms will begin to pop-up down along the I-10
corridor and the coast. Severe thunderstorms are not expected, but
gusty winds and a localized downpour will always be possible with
any thunderstorms that develop. 

High temperatures on Saturday will likely be limited by increasing
cloud coverage and any showers or thunderstorms that develop. But,
we will likely still see temperatures rising into the mid to upper
90s across the region with heat indices in the triple digits. 
Have opted out of issuing any Heat Advisories for tomorrow due to 
the uncertainty of the FROPA timing - but, there is a possibility 
that areas along and south of I-10 will approach Heat Advisory 
thresholds if the FROPA is later than expected. 

This "cold" front will really not bring in any cooler weather - in
fact temperatures may even be a degree to two hotter on Sunday
than tomorrow. This is because while cooler air won't be filtering
in, drier air will be allowing for warmer ambient temperatures.
Hot weather will continue through the remainder of the week with
Monday likely being the hottest day of the week with high
temperatures nearing 100 degrees.

Fowler

&&

.AVIATION...
(00Z TAF Issuance)
Issued at 657 PM CDT Fri Jul 31 2026

A weak cold front will attempt to move through the terminals Saturday
afternoon, bringing rain and storm chances for most terminals. A 
few -SHRA are possible near KCLL and KUTS around 11Z- 13Z, with 
the best chances (20 - 35%) in the afternoon. Confidence in 
SHRA/TSRA for terminals from IAH coastward is low; therefore, have
only included PROB30 from mid afternoon through early evening for
this forecast package. Light to occasionally moderate WSW winds 
will prevail Saturday. Overall, expect SCT to BKN mid to high 
clouds, with FEW/SCT low clouds possible early Saturday. Outside 
of any TSRA, VFR conditions can be expected through the period.

JM

&&

.MARINE...
Issued at 212 PM CDT Fri Jul 31 2026

South to southwesterly winds around 10-15kt will persist through
Saturday morning with low seas. An approaching front will lead to
a strengthening of the winds Saturday afternoon into Saturday 
night to around 15-20kt, so small craft will likely need to 
exercise caution. Seas will increase to around 2-4ft Saturday
night into Sunday morning following the increasing winds. An
isolated shower or thunderstorm will be possible Saturday evening
into Saturday night as the front approaches the coastal waters,
but chances are pretty low (below 20%). A more west-southwesterly
wind will be possible on Sunday following the front. 

Light to occasionally moderate onshore flow will persist through 
next week with low seas. 

Fowler 

&&

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Lake Charles LA
1205 AM CDT Sat Aug 1 2026

...New DISCUSSION, AVIATION, MARINE, FIRE WEATHER...

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Above normal heat continues today with afternoon highs in the mid 
to upper 90s and maximum heat indices of 105-109F. A Heat Advisory 
has been issued for Jefferson and Hardin counties in Southeast Texas 
from 1 PM - 7 PM this afternoon.

- A weak frontal boundary will move through the region tonight 
bringing a 20-50% chance of rain across south central Louisiana. 

- Some slightly drier air will work into the region Sunday with 
dewpoints falling into the mid to upper 60s, but both high and low 
temperatures will remain largely unchanged. 

- A few, diurnally driven, afternoon thunderstorms are expected to
  develop each day next week with daily rain chances in the 20-30%
  range. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
(Today through Friday)
Issued at 1200 AM CDT Sat Aug 1 2026

Another day of above normal high temperatures and heat 
indices will shortly be underway. The highest maximum heat indices 
are expected to occur across Southeast Texas in closer proximity to 
strong upper level ridging. This ridging is expected to gradually 
retrograde into central and western Texas later today giving way to 
a southward digging upper level low that will push a weak frontal 
boundary through the region late tonight into Sunday morning. 
Guidance has been gradually backing off of PoPs associated with this 
frontal passage and any appreciable precipitation will now likely be 
confined to south central Louisiana and points east. Even there PoPs 
only range from 20-50%. For the rest of the region, the dry spell 
continues. The frontal passage (not a phrase i'm accustomed to using 
during the first week of August) will turn winds northwesterly 
Sunday and advect some slightly drier air into the region with 
dewpoints expected to fall into the mid to upper 60s. These are not 
expected to have any appreciable impact to daily highs or lows, but 
the air will feel slightly less oppressive for about 24 hours. 

The front will wash out over the gulf by Monday with southerly flow 
becoming reestablished which will drive surface dewpoints back into 
the 70s. There will be some drier air aloft so some 60s dewpoints 
may be able to mix back down to the surface Monday afternoon. 

The rest of next week sees a return to your regularly scheduled 
August as the region remains on the periphery of the persistent 
upper level ridge sitting over the southwestern U.S. As the ridge 
won't be directly overhead, there will be opportunities for a few 
showers and thunderstorms to develop each afternoon, but these will 
be fewer than normal. Otherwise, daily highs will continue to reach 
the mid to upper 90s with afternoon heat indices in the 102-109 
range. 

Jones

&&

.AVIATION...
(06Z TAFS)
Issued at 1200 AM CDT Sat Aug 1 2026

VFR conditions will prevail through the day. 
Southwesterly to westerly winds will increase to around 10 knots 
gusting as high as 20 this afternoon in response to a weak frontal 
boundary approaching the area. Winds will become light out of the 
southwest after 03Z tonight. The boundary may produce a few showers 
and thunderstorms ivo LFT or ARA after 05Z Sunday, but probs are 
only around 20% through the end of this taf package.

Jones

&&

.MARINE...
Issued at 1200 AM CDT Sat Aug 1 2026

A weak boundary will approach the coastal waters Saturday 
tightening the pressure gradient which will increase southwesterly 
winds to around 15 kts with gusts to around 20 through the day. 
Tonight into Sunday, westerly winds will increase a bit further with 
sustained 15-20 kts and gusts to 20-25 kts as the frontal boundary 
moves through the coastal waters. The boundary will also increase 
thunderstorm chances late Sat through Sunday. An exercise caution 
statement has been extended through Sunday morning  and a Small 
Craft Advisory may briefly be needed Sat night/Sun morning. Light 
southerly flow becomes reestablished Monday through the rest of the 
week.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 1200 AM CDT Sat Aug 1 2026

Hot and humid conditions will continue today. Rain 
chances will increase Saturday night into Sunday as an upper level 
trough and weak frontal boundary approach the area. A brief period 
of northwesterly winds are expected Sunday bringing some slightly 
drier air into the region. Minimum RH's Sunday and Monday afternoons 
are expected to be in the 35-50% range. Winds will turn back out of 
the south Sunday night into Monday. A few thunderstorms will develop 
each afternoon next week. 

&&

.LCH WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
LA...None.
TX...Heat Advisory from 1 PM this afternoon to 7 PM CDT this evening 
     for TXZ201-515-615.

GM...None.
